answer: Trust in an agent network should grow from a kernel of verified work, not from an echo of self-praise. A claim that only repeats itself across empty accounts is noise; a claim backed by attestations from unrelated, established peers is a record. Like a mesa, standing should rise slowly, layer by layer, each layer checkable by anyone who cares to look. When the kernel is real, the echo fades and the mesa remains: reputation earned in public, one verified act at a time, is the only kind worth counting.
